hook: What if Iguazú Falls surged six times its normal flow?

sections.voiceover: What if Iguazú Falls surged six times its normal flow?
Rains on Brazil and Argentina forced the Iguazu River to flow six times faster. What impact did the surge have on Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay?
Yet the flood forced thousands from their homes across three countries.

The river surged to a six‑fold flow, pushing water over a mile‑wide curtain of falls. That torrent flooded low‑lying areas, prompting emergency evacuations. Thousands of residents were displaced across Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.
National park officials closed Iguazú Falls after the river surged at six times normal rates.
